_doc: Made by `mac/pcjob pair`; copy to config.json only to set things by hand. config.json is personal (gitignored).
_pc_os_doc: windows (default: the PC runs pc/ scripts), linux (a PC set up with linux/setup-linux.sh; pc_root is then /srv/lazylink and the ssh user lazylink; `pcjob pair --os linux` sets both) or mac (an Apple Silicon Mac set up with macpc/setup-mac.sh; pc_root is then ~lazylink/lazylink and the ssh user lazylink; `pcjob pair --os mac` sets both). See docs/MAC-PC.md for what is tested.

extra_model_folders._doc: optional: model folders you already have on the PC (ComfyUI layout), read-only, so nothing downloads twice

cheap_hours_note: optional: when power is cheapest (this computer's clock), e.g. your utility's time-of-use plan name and where you checked it
_cheap_hours_auto_doc: optional: true = your AI agent looks up your utility's cheapest hours for your area (asks you once which utility/area) and keeps cheap_hours current
_cheap_feed_doc: optional: a free live price feed picks the cheapest hours of each day instead of cheap_hours. Add the line {"source": "comed"} (ComEd, Northern Illinois) or {"source": "octopus", "region": "C"} (Octopus Agile, UK; region is your letter A-P). cheap_hours stays the fallback if the feed is down, so keep it set.
_cheap_feed_hours_doc: optional, with cheap_feed: how many of the cheapest hours to use in each 24 h (1-24, default 6)
